title: Empty first auth-param
explanation: A comma sits between the scheme and the first auth-param, as in 'Bearer , resource_metadata="..."'. It is what you get when a script appends ', resource_metadata=...' to a challenge that had no params.
clientBreaks: Reported once in an earlier internal demo: LM Studio's MCP bridge failed with 'authentication required' on this shape while the same client completed discovery on the correct shapes. Not re-measured here, so for any other client this is UNVERIFIED.
fix: Use a space after the scheme when there are no params yet ('Bearer resource_metadata="..."') and a comma only between params.
rfcNote: Whether the leading comma is strictly illegal is arguable: the list rule lets recipients ignore empty list elements. Strict parsers reject it anyway. UNVERIFIED reading of the RFC, from memory.

title: Empty element in the param list
explanation: Two commas in a row, or a trailing comma. Lenient parsers skip it.
clientBreaks: UNVERIFIED: strict parsers may reject it; lenient ones accept it.

title: Unterminated quoted string
explanation: A value opened with a double quote and never closed it, so everything after it is swallowed into the value.
clientBreaks: UNVERIFIED which clients; no parser can recover the params after the quote.
fix: Close the quote; escape an inner quote as \".

title: Unquoted value that is not a token
explanation: A value written without quotes contains characters a token cannot hold, such as ':' or '/' in a URL. URLs must be quoted.
clientBreaks: UNVERIFIED: a strict parser stops at the first such character; a lenient one reads to the next comma.
fix: Wrap the value in double quotes.

title: Not a name=value pair, or no comma between params
explanation: An element in the param list is a bare word, or two params are separated by a space instead of a comma.
clientBreaks: UNVERIFIED which clients; most split on commas and would see one malformed param.
fix: Write name="value" pairs separated by commas.

title: 401 without resource_metadata
explanation: An MCP client that follows RFC 9728 learns where the protected-resource metadata lives from the resource_metadata param. Without it the client has to guess a well-known URL or give up.
clientBreaks: UNVERIFIED: depends on whether a client falls back to the well-known path. Some may; the lab does not know which.

title: resource_metadata is not https
explanation: The metadata URL must use https, except that a loopback address is tolerated while testing (see WA008).
clientBreaks: UNVERIFIED: clients may refuse to fetch an http metadata URL.
fix: Serve the metadata over https and use that URL.

title: resource_metadata is http on a loopback host
explanation: http is fine for a laptop test, but this URL would be rejected anywhere else.
clientBreaks: UNVERIFIED.

title: resource_metadata is not a usable absolute URL
explanation: The value is empty, relative, has a fragment, carries a user name or password, or cannot be parsed as a URL.
clientBreaks: UNVERIFIED: a client cannot fetch a relative URL without guessing its base.
fix: Give the full absolute URL with no fragment and no credentials.

title: resource_metadata path is not the usual well-known path
explanation: The URL does not contain /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource. Custom paths are allowed, but most deployments use the well-known one.
clientBreaks: UNVERIFIED: none expected.
fix: Check that the URL really serves the metadata document.

title: Unknown error code
explanation: The error value is not one of invalid_request, invalid_token or insufficient_scope (the Bearer codes), nor one of the DPoP codes use_dpop_nonce and invalid_dpop_proof.
clientBreaks: UNVERIFIED: clients usually ignore an unknown code but cannot act on it.

title: error_description has characters outside the allowed set
explanation: The text holds a non-ASCII or control character, or a bare double quote or backslash. The Bearer RFC limits these.
clientBreaks: UNVERIFIED.
fix: Keep it to printable ASCII without quotes or backslashes.

title: error_uri is not an absolute URL
explanation: error_uri should point to a human-readable page and be an absolute URI.
clientBreaks: UNVERIFIED.
fix: Use an absolute https URL or drop it.

title: scope value is malformed
explanation: scope must be space-separated scope tokens. An empty value, commas instead of spaces, or characters such as a double quote are signs of a mistake.
clientBreaks: UNVERIFIED: a client may ask the authorization server for one scope named 'a,b'.

title: 401 carrying insufficient_scope
explanation: insufficient_scope means 'I know who you are, but this token lacks the scope', which is a 403. A 401 tells the client to authenticate again.
clientBreaks: UNVERIFIED: a client may loop re-authenticating when the real fix is a wider scope request.
fix: Return 403 with error="insufficient_scope" and the required scope.

title: 403 carrying invalid_token
explanation: An invalid, expired or revoked token is a 401 so the client knows to refresh or sign in again.
clientBreaks: UNVERIFIED: a client may not try to refresh on a 403.

title: 403 insufficient_scope without scope
explanation: The RFC lets the server name the scope that is needed. Without it the client cannot step up; it can only fail.
clientBreaks: UNVERIFIED: step-up flows need this value.

title: error code on a request that carried no credentials
explanation: When the request had no token at all the server should send the bare challenge, not invalid_token, so the client starts discovery instead of treating it as a bad token.
clientBreaks: UNVERIFIED: a client may try to refresh a token it never had.
fix: Drop error and error_description on the no-credentials 401.

title: 401 with no WWW-Authenticate header
explanation: A 401 response must carry a challenge. Without one the client has nothing to start from.
clientBreaks: UNVERIFIED: clients show a generic failure.

title: Duplicate auth-param
explanation: The same param name appears twice in one challenge. The Bearer RFC says each attribute must not appear more than once.
clientBreaks: UNVERIFIED: parsers keep the first, the last, or fail; they disagree.

title: More than one challenge
explanation: Several schemes are offered in one header. That is legal, but a client that reads only the first challenge sees only that one.
clientBreaks: UNVERIFIED.
fix: Offer Bearer first if Bearer is what clients must use.

title: Bearer is not the first challenge
explanation: Another scheme comes first. Clients that only read the first challenge will not see the Bearer one.
clientBreaks: UNVERIFIED which clients read only the first.

title: No Bearer challenge
explanation: The header has challenges but none is Bearer, so an OAuth client has nothing to act on.
clientBreaks: UNVERIFIED.

title: More than one WWW-Authenticate header line
explanation: Challenges are split across header lines. Some stacks fold them, some keep only the first or last.
clientBreaks: UNVERIFIED: depends on the HTTP client.

title: Header too long to lint
explanation: The lab stops at 8192 characters. Real servers and proxies cap header size too, often lower.
clientBreaks: UNVERIFIED: limits differ per proxy.

title: No auth-scheme
explanation: A challenge must start with a scheme token such as Bearer.
clientBreaks: UNVERIFIED.

title: Bearer challenge with a bare token instead of params
explanation: 'Bearer abc' is the token68 form, used for credentials. A Bearer challenge carries name=value params.
clientBreaks: UNVERIFIED.

title: invalid_request on a 401 or 403
explanation: invalid_request describes a malformed request, which the Bearer RFC pairs with 400.
clientBreaks: UNVERIFIED.

title: Metadata document is not a JSON object
explanation: RFC 9728 metadata is a JSON object.
clientBreaks: UNVERIFIED.

title: resource missing or not an https URL
explanation: The resource member names the protected resource and must be an https URL with no fragment.
clientBreaks: UNVERIFIED.
fix: Set resource to the resource's https identifier.

title: resource does not match the identifier it was fetched for
explanation: A client that fetched metadata for one resource must reject a document that names another. A mismatch is how a stray or hostile document gets rejected.
clientBreaks: UNVERIFIED: compliant clients refuse the document.
fix: Make resource identical to the resource identifier.

title: authorization_servers missing or malformed
explanation: It is optional in the RFC, but an MCP client needs it to know which authorization server to use. It must be a list of https issuer URLs.
clientBreaks: UNVERIFIED.

title: scopes_supported is not a list of strings
explanation: scopes_supported is a JSON list of scope strings.
clientBreaks: UNVERIFIED.

title: bearer_methods_supported has an unknown value
explanation: The values are header, body and query.
clientBreaks: UNVERIFIED.
